description: Install Auth.js v5 (next-auth@beta) and add a build-safe Google OAuth configuration with role resolution. This establishes the auth foundation: a lazily/at-request-time-configured NextAuth instance with the Google provider, a JWT session strategy (no DB adapter, so no build-time DB dependency), a role resolver that maps a signed-in Google email to a UserRoleCode, and a role-aware session helper for server code. Absence of Google/secret env vars must NOT break `next build` or `npm run typecheck`.
steps: From web/, run `npm install next-auth@beta` (Auth.js v5 for Next.js 15 App Router). Commit the updated package.json and package-lock.json.

Create web/lib/auth/roles.ts: a pure, side-effect-free module that resolves a UserRoleCode for a given email. Resolution order: (1) exact case-insensitive match against DEFAULT_USERS in web/data/seed.ts (use that user's role); (2) allowlist env vars — ADMIN_EMAILS -> SUPER_ADMIN, TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS -> TEST_ADMIN, REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS -> REPORT_REVIEWER (each a comma/space-separated list of emails, matched case-insensitively; highest privilege wins if an email appears in more than one); (3) default to STUDENT. Export `resolveRoleForEmail(email: string): UserRoleCode` and a helper `isStaffRole(role: UserRoleCode): boolean` that reuses USER_ROLES[role].isStaff from web/lib/riasec/types.ts. Read env vars at call time (process.env.*), never at module top-level, so the build stays env-free.

Create web/lib/auth/config.ts (or web/auth.ts, whichever fits the NextAuth v5 convention you choose — document the choice): initialize NextAuth with the Google provider. Read GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / AUTH_SECRET at request time, NOT at module load. Guard missing config: expose `isAuthConfigured(): boolean` (true only when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and AUTH_SECRET are all set). Use session strategy 'jwt' (no database adapter — this keeps the build/runtime free of a DB requirement). In the `jwt` callback, on first sign-in resolve the role via resolveRoleForEmail(user.email) and store `role` on the token; in the `session` callback, expose `session.user.role` and `session.user.email`. Export the NextAuth handlers { GET, POST }, plus `auth`, `signIn`, `signOut`.
Create the route handler web/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts that re-exports the GET and POST handlers from the auth config. Include `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` if needed for compatibility.

Augment NextAuth types so `session.user.role` (UserRoleCode) and the token `role` are typed. Add a web/types/next-auth.d.ts (module augmentation) or inline declaration; ensure `npm run typecheck` passes.

Add a server-only helper web/lib/auth/session.ts exporting `getCurrentUser()` (returns { email, role } | null from the NextAuth `auth()` session) and `requireStaff()` / `requireRole(roles: UserRoleCode[])` style helpers that return a structured result ({ ok: boolean; error?: string; user?: ... }) usable by server actions and route handlers. When auth is NOT configured (isAuthConfigured() === false), decide and document the fallback behavior consistent with FEAT-002 (see that feature's steps). Keep all user-facing error strings in Spanish.
acceptance_criteria: `npm install next-auth@beta` succeeded and package.json lists next-auth in dependencies; package-lock.json updated.
web/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts exists and exports GET and POST.

resolveRoleForEmail returns the seed user's role for a DEFAULT_USERS email, honors ADMIN_EMAILS/TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS/REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS allowlists, and defaults to STUDENT otherwise — all reading env at call time.
isAuthConfigured() returns false when Google/secret env vars are unset and true when all are set.
`npm run typecheck` passes with NO env vars set.
`npm run build` succeeds with NO env vars set.
verification: From web/: run `npm run typecheck` and confirm it passes.
From web/: run `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" npm run build` (a clean env with no secrets) and confirm the build completes successfully.
From web/: run `npm run test -- --run` and confirm the existing 48 tests still pass (this feature should not break them).
findings: Installed next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32 (Auth.js v5). Files added: web/auth.ts (chose the official v5 `auth.ts` at web root convention; route handler re-exports { GET, POST } from it), web/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts (exports GET/POST + runtime='nodejs'), web/lib/auth/roles.ts (resolveRoleForEmail + isStaffRole, env read at call time), web/lib/auth/session.ts (getCurrentUser, requireStaff, requireRole returning structured {ok, authConfigured, error?, user?}), web/types/next-auth.d.ts (module augmentation). Build-safety: NextAuth is initialized with a CONFIG FUNCTION so secrets are read per-request; the Google provider is only added when isAuthConfigured() is true (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID + GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET + AUTH_SECRET all set), otherwise providers=[] so build/typecheck pass with no env. Session strategy 'jwt', no DB adapter. Role resolved in jwt callback via resolveRoleForEmail and exposed on session.user.role. IMPORTANT typing note for FEAT-002: JWT augmentation had to target BOTH `next-auth/jwt` AND `@auth/core/jwt` (the latter is where the JWT interface is actually defined; augmenting only next-auth/jwt left token.role typed as {}). Fallback decision for FEAT-002: when isAuthConfigured()===false, getCurrentUser() returns null and requireStaff/requireRole return {ok:false, authConfigured:false, ...}; this module does NOT itself open access. FEAT-002 must decide whether to preserve the current staff.ts demo-mode (open access when unconfigured) using the exposed authConfigured flag. Verification passed: npm run typecheck OK, `env -i` clean build OK (route /api/auth/[...nextauth] present), npm run lint OK, all 48 tests still pass.
